name: Game theory

subjectOf.text: The Folk Theorems of game theory imply that no matter how complicated a stable coin protocol becomes, a powerful and patient player has strategies to subvert the system and profit at the expense of the group.
subjectOf.abstract: No matter how complicated the protocols become for creating a stable coin, there are strategies that a powerful and patient player can use to subvert the system to profit at the expense of the group
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies - First Order Principles (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3402701
scope_conditions: any fixed protocol, however complex

subjectOf.text: For any static set of rules in an infinitely repeated game using reputation stakes there is a way to subvert the rules for individual profit at the expense of the group, a result the author attributes to the Folk Theorems of game theory.
subjectOf.abstract: For any static set of rules in an infinitely repeated game using reputation (stakes), there is a way to subvert the rules for an individual's profit at the expense of the group.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization - A Primer on the New Economy (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3406323
scope_conditions: infinitely repeated games using reputation or stakes
static rule sets

subjectOf.text: For any static set of rules in an infinitely repeated game using reputation stakes, there is a way to subvert the rules for an individual's profit at the expense of the group, which is why static decentralized governance rules can always be gamed and only dynamic, changing rules can address the problem.
subjectOf.abstract: For any static set of rules in an infinitely repeated game using reputation (stakes), there is a way to subvert the rules for an individual's profit at the expense of the group.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization - Past, Present, and Future (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411897
scope_conditions: infinitely repeated games with reputation or stake based rules
static rule sets

subjectOf.text: The Folk Theorems of game theory prove that any rules that can be formally set down can be subverted: strategies always exist that follow the rules and still allow a minority player to profit at the expense of the majority.
subjectOf.abstract: The Folk Theorems of Game Theory (explained in Chapter ^) prove the point that any rules that can be formally set down can be subverted. Strategies al- ways exist which follow the rules and yet allow a minority player to profit at the ex- pense of the majority.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Introduction to Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782192
scope_conditions: any formally specified rule set analyzed as a repeated game

subjectOf.text: No set of written rules can be made complete: the Folk Theorems demonstrate that however rules are written, strategies exist that follow those rules yet profit the individual at the expense of the group, so a perfect secular constitution is impossible.
subjectOf.abstract: The Folk theories demonstrate that how- ever the rules are written, strategies exist which follow the rules, yet profit the indi- vidual at the expense of the group.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Historical Sketches of Centralization vs. Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782193
scope_conditions: any static, formally specified set of rules governing a group

subjectOf.text: Honesty would be the wrong strategy for an agent if the contract were anonymous and its resolution did not affect future contracts, because that situation is a single-stage zero-sum game in which stealing all the entrusted wealth is optimal.
subjectOf.abstract: Honesty would be a bad strategy for the agent if the contract was anonymous and the resolution didn't affect future contracts.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Historical Sketches of Centralization vs. Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782193
scope_conditions: anonymous contracting
no effect of the outcome on future business

subjectOf.text: Adding reputation to the contracting game converts it from a single-stage zero-sum game into a repeated positive-sum game in which the rest of the community becomes relevant, because reputation is a future-oriented commodity that pays off with the promise of future contracts.
subjectOf.abstract: By adding reputation to the game, it becomes a repeated game, and the rest of the community becomes relevant. Reputation is a future-oriented commodity, which pays off profits with the promise of future contracts. Now the game is a repeated game which is positive-sum.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Historical Sketches of Centralization vs. Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782193
scope_conditions: networks where reputation is observable and policed by the community

subjectOf.text: For any game, a new assumption can be added that generalizes the game so that the previous winning strategy becomes a losing strategy and a new winning strategy arises; the authors offer this as a meta-theorem that cannot itself be formalized.
subjectOf.abstract: No matter which game you are playing, you can add a new assumption to make a more complicated generalization of the game, so that the previous winning strategy becomes a losing strategy, and a new winning strategy arises.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, A Technical Perspective on Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782203
scope_conditions: any formal game model
actors free to change their behavior and desires

subjectOf.text: Keeping decentralized networks running productively requires a dynamic design with checks and balances combined with the incentive design insights of game theory.
subjectOf.abstract: A dynamic design with checks and balances and the incentive design insights of game theory are necessary to keep these networks running productively.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Eight Institutions for the Evolution of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782205
scope_conditions: applies to decentralized networks intended to operate over time

subjectOf.text: Reputation changes the incentive structure of a decentralized organization from a single stage, zero sum game into a repeated positive sum game, which is why the authors treat reputation as the key to effective decentralized governance.
subjectOf.abstract: Reputation changes the incentive structure from a single-stage, zero-sum game to a repeated positive-sum game.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Governance (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782214
scope_conditions: the reputation system is formally linked to the organization's profits

subjectOf.text: A DAO that relies on a centralized oracle will eventually be exploited, because the people controlling the oracle will become aware of their power over automated contract triggers and, given the competitive nature of capitalism, are right to take advantage of it.
subjectOf.abstract: Eventually, the people who have the relevant power in the centralized oracle will become aware of the power they have over the DAO. Eventually there will be an opportunity to exploit that information.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of History In Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782217
scope_conditions: DAO automated by smart contracts on oracle data
sufficient value at stake

subjectOf.text: From a game theory perspective the open source culture advocated in the Web3 movement is not sustainable in the long term unless it is married with a culture of respect for history.
subjectOf.abstract: the current open source culture advocated in the WebM movement is not sustainable in the long term. Unless we marry it with a culture of respect for history.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of History In Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782217
scope_conditions: long term horizon
absence of a culture acknowledging past contributions

subjectOf.text: Review changes the game theoretical perspective from a single stage game to a repeated game, which produces more efficient cooperation instead of internal competition and is what makes the open source environment sustainable in the long run.
subjectOf.abstract: Review changes the game theoretical perspective from a single stage game, to a repeated game. This leads to more efficient cooperation instead of internal compe- tition.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of History In Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782217
scope_conditions: DAOs where past contributions remain reviewable

subjectOf.text: Transcendental values are necessary for long-term stability because every formal, explicitly specified protocol is permanently exposed to strategies that subvert it, a result the authors draw from the Folk Theorems of game theory.
subjectOf.abstract: By the insights gleaned from the Folk Theo- rems of Game Theory, transcendental values are necessary to maintain long-term sta- bility in the face of ever-present strategies for subverting any formal, explicitly-speci- fied protocol.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of Transcendental Unifying Values for Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782220
scope_conditions: long-term stability
formally specified protocols

subjectOf.text: Charging an admission fee disincentivizes betrayal and defection, because the sunk cost of joining makes cheating expensive when rejoining would also be expensive even under anonymity.
subjectOf.abstract: The DAO of DAOs disincentivizes betrayal and defection by charging an admission fee to become a DAO of DAOs member. Given the sunk cost of joining the DAO of DAOs, it is more expensive for prospective members to cheat because it would be expensive to rejoin even if members could be anonymous.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, A Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) of DAOs (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3799320
scope_conditions: members who can be blacklisted
anonymous membership

subjectOf.text: Charging an admission or denial of service fee to become a voting associate disincentivizes betrayal and defection, because the sunk cost of joining makes cheating expensive even where associates can remain anonymous.
subjectOf.abstract: - The CHARITYxDAO disincentivize betrayal and defection by charging an admission fee, ie. DoS fee to become a CHARITYxDAO VA. Given the sunk cost of joining the CHARITYxDAO, it is more expensive for prospective VAs to cheat because it would be expensive to rejoin even if VAs could be anonymous.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Optimize Charitable Giving (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3981021
scope_conditions: DAO membership with paid admission and blacklisting

subjectOf.text: Slashing establishes a Nash equilibrium in which rational validators adhere to honest behavior, because the expected cost of penalties exceeds any short-term gain available from misconduct.

subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Cryptographic Foundations and Interdisciplinary Dimensions of the Secure Proof of Stake (SPoS) Conse (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5225296

subjectOf.text: Weighted voting creates a Nash equilibrium favoring honest participation, because creating additional Sybil identities yields no extra voting power absent corresponding contributions.

subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Cryptographic Foundations and Interdisciplinary Dimensions of the Secure Proof of Stake (SPoS) Conse (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5225296

subjectOf.text: Collusion calls for a different remedy than Sybil attacks: adaptive slashing that detects coordinated deviations through statistical anomaly detection is what deters group manipulation.
subjectOf.abstract: For collusion, adaptive slashing—detecting coordinated deviations via statistical anomaly detection—deters group manipulation, drawing on game-theoretic deterrence
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Cryptographic Foundations and Interdisciplinary Dimensions of the Secure Proof of Stake (SPoS) Conse (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5225296

subjectOf.text: Nash's model, by presuming homo economicus unbound, overestimates human computational capacity and perpetuates a normative ideal that distorts policy and institutional design by justifying frictionless markets that never materialize in human systems.

subjectOf.text: Under the standard citation-weighted payment formulation the dominant strategy for a self-interested agent is to cite no one and maximize self-attribution, which is the precise negation of honest knowledge attribution.
